prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall state and the Z2 topological classification of insulators, and for its first experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B028 as a single-part prize to Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. Having read all eight first-round statements, the case still rests on what I understand the committee to ask of a prize, a discovery or invention with identifiable people behind the original work. Here a compact theoretical step (the quantum spin Hall state and the Z2 invariant) was followed by a decisive first realisation (edge transport in HgTe quantum wells), and the concept then spread to three-dimensional materials, photonics and computational materials searches. From my own field I can add that the interpretation has been tested by independent transport, ARPES, STM and imaging experiments over fifteen to twenty years, so the maturity question is closed in a way it is not for B046 or for the redefinition-dependent part of B034. The round-1 exchange also moved Danielsson to the same trio, so the Mele-versus-Hasan question is less open than it looked after the opening ballots. I would word the citation around the 2D prediction-plus-first-realisation chain and say in the citation text that the three-dimensional work followed from it, so the prize does not claim more than its three names can carry.
statement.case_against: The attribution weakness is real and I do not think the committee should minimise it. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed HgTe and thereby motivated Molenkamp's experiment; Fu, Kane and Mele and Moore and Balents opened the 3D branch; Hasan made the first ARPES identification. None of these can be credited under a three-person cap, and any citation must be written so that it is accurate about what is and is not being honoured. Lindroth's point about the 2016 prize is also a legitimate reason to hesitate, although I read that prize as honouring topological phase transitions and quantum Hall precursors rather than the protected edge and surface states of insulating band structures. If the committee decides that the omissions make the credit misrepresent who did the original work, B034 is the cleaner configuration and I would accept it without reservation about the physics, as its attribution is the clearest on the shortlist. I would still prefer to wait on B046 until the pairing mechanism and the twist-angle reproducibility are better understood.

responses.point: Danielsson moved in his round-1 response from Kane, Molenkamp and Hasan to Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, while still regarding Hasan's 3D identification as decisive for the field and asking that the citation not present the 2D result as the whole discovery.
responses.response: I welcome the move and I think it settles the largest attribution question inside B028. On your remaining concern, I would not pretend the citation can cover both branches with three names. The 2D chain, Kane and Mele's proposal and Molenkamp's HgTe observation, is the one that has a single theory-experiment line. A citation that names the quantum spin Hall state, the Z2 classification and the first HgTe realisation is accurate as it stands; I would add only a general reference to the topological insulator concept so that nothing implies the 3D materials did not matter. Hasan's ARPES work is the best experimental argument for the 3D branch, and I value it as a spectroscopist, but putting him in means taking out either Mele or Molenkamp, and each of those removals misstates the origin more than the omission of Hasan does.

responses.point: Lindroth prefers B034 with a clean two-name credit and argues that the 2016 prize on topological phases overlaps with B028 more than Danielsson and others allow, and that B028 has a contested credit while B034 has none.
responses.response: I take the overlap argument more seriously than I did in round 1, but I still do not think it decides the matter. The 2016 citation was about topological phase transitions and phases of matter in the Thouless, Haldane and Kosterlitz sense, and the quantum Hall precursors. Z2 classification of time-reversal-invariant insulators and the protected edge states of spin-orbit-coupled band structures are a different result with a different experimental line, and no one on the 2016 list is credited for them. I would expect the citation to say plainly that it concerns insulators with protected boundary states and not the earlier work. Your point that a two-name credit has no forced exclusion is the strongest part of the B034 case and I treat it as a real difference between the candidates. My difference with you is that an allocation problem in B028 is a problem of naming people for the same idea, which a citation can handle, whereas B034 is more of a precision advance in an established technique, and I weigh the novelty of the physical regime more.

responses.point: Kroll proposes B034 for Katori and Ye, treating the pending redefinition of the second as supporting context, and has disclosed possible proximity to the Hall laboratory environment around Ye.
responses.response: I agree with the chair's reading that your disclosure is best handled by recording it and letting the committee weigh it, and I do not think it undermines your scientific argument, which stands on independent clock comparisons and on the 10^-18 results. I differ on the weight to give the redefinition. If the committee wants the clocks to be recognised for what has been demonstrated, then there is no reason to wait for the metrology bodies; if it wants them recognised because of the redefinition, the timing argument becomes weaker, because the prize would then depend on an administrative decision. I accept that B034 is the best fallback, and I accept that early lattice-clock groups may have claims, but a two-name credit is defensible if the citation names the scheme and the accuracy achieved. My preference for B028 is about the size of the conceptual step, and I do not think the committee loses anything essential by choosing B034 if it concludes that B028 cannot be credited cleanly.

responses.point: Mehlig prefers B046 with MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Andrei and argues that a citation built on flat bands and correlated phases avoids resting the prize on the unsettled pairing mechanism, while granting that B028 is the safer choice on timing.
responses.response: A citation framed around flat bands and correlated insulating states is a sensible way to avoid the mechanism question, and I agree that the prediction-then-experiment structure is a real strength. My concern is that maturity affects more than the citation. The experiments are about eight years old, the sample-to-sample dependence on twist angle and strain is well known to people who image these structures, and the superconducting phase is still the part most people associate with the discovery. On attribution I find your choice of Andrei over Bistritzer defensible, since her STM and transport evidence is independent of the continuum model, but it still leaves Cao, the first author of the 2018 work, outside the credit. You say B028 is the safer choice on timing and I think that is the deciding point this year; I would keep B046 as a strong candidate for a later cycle and keep it as my second alternative.

responses.point: Pearce, as chair, proposes a two-part prize combining B034 (Katori and Ye) with B005 (Halzen alone), and himself says the one-name credit is the weakest element and that the astroparticle part falls away if it cannot be defended.
responses.response: Thank you for being candid about the weakness in B005. I agree with your own assessment: a single-name credit for a collaboration of hundreds, with AMANDA and the detector and analysis teams outside the credited names, is difficult to defend, and Kroll's question about who made the first statistically decisive observation has no good answer in the supplied names. That leaves your proposal as B034 alone, and I would then compare it to B028 directly. A two-part prize also has a practical problem, since it leaves only one slot for a second part when B028 and B046 each need three names, so it works against the candidates that have the most support. I would not support combining unrelated fields only to fill the prize.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat the omission of Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu, Moore, Balents and Hasan as acceptable once the citation states plainly what the three names are credited for.
Whether the 2016 prize on topological phases and phase transitions will be read as having already covered topological insulators, which Lindroth and Mehlig treat as a reason to wait.
Whether the redefinition of the second, if it occurs, would change my ordering of B028 and B034; at present I treat it as supporting evidence only.
I have not independently verified priority details beyond what the shortlist and the round-1 statements state.
statement.conflict_note: Unchanged from round 1. None of the credited names for B028 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp, Hasan) appears among my documented connections, and I have no documented tie to the names on B034 or B046. I share a Chalmers affiliation with Johansson, who also prefers B028 with the same trio; the chair's summary records this, and I consider it an institutional colleague link and not a stake in the candidates. I note Kroll's disclosure concerning B034 and think it should be handled by transparency.
